ldfreq

Lexical diversity, vocabulary profiles and corpus comparisons in R. Keep the original text, token choices, reference coverage and measurement settings connected to the results you report.

Guides · Function reference · Metric selection · Issues

Install

Install the fixed release 1.0.0 below (R 4.1 or later).

install.packages(c("digest", "stringi"))
install.packages(
  "https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq/releases/download/v1.0.0/ldfreq_1.0.0.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL, type = "source"
)
library(ldfreq)

Optional integrations state their additional packages in the relevant guide. Use browseVignettes("ldfreq") for guides matching your installed version. Earlier releases remain available in the release archive.

Start with your text 

text <- paste(
  "Students compared two versions of a short story in their writing class.",
  "They marked repeated words and discussed how each writer introduced new ideas.",
  "One group revised the opening while another group examined the ending.",
  "After reading the stories again, the students explained their choices and",
  "saved both the original texts and their revised versions for later comparison."
)
result <- lexdiv_metrics_text(text, tokenizer = "english", case = "lower",
  metrics = c("mattr", "hdd", "mtld"))
result$results[c("metric_id", "value", "N", "status", "missing_reason")]

# Check counted words, make a report table, and retain the full analysis.
head(result$token_audit)
report <- lexdiv_widen(result$results,
  values_from = c("value", "status", "missing_reason", "N"))
report
saveRDS(list(text = text, analysis = result, report = report), "analysis.rds")

This connects text → scores and counted words → report table → saved record. Reopen it with readRDS("analysis.rds"); the full record retains information that a values-only table would lose. The first-analysis guide extends this to several documents, missing scores and a plot.

Use lexdiv_metrics(tokens, ...) for an already ordered character vector of words, and lexdiv_metrics_text_batch() for multiple named texts. Inspect status and missing_reason: an unavailable score is not zero. Keep window and sample sizes fixed when comparing documents.

Choose a measure for your question

For local lexical variety, start with MATTR at a fixed window size. Our evidence covers English surface words at window 50; check its consistency for your material, especially short texts. Use HD-D at a fixed sample size when the distribution of word frequencies, rather than local sequence, is the target. MTLD and MTLD-MA measure factor lengths and need particular care with short texts. TTR is useful at a controlled length; it is strongly affected by length otherwise.

The metric-selection guide explains these choices using published research and PELIC, ICNALE, OANC and BAWE results, including length sensitivity, sampling agreement, missing scores and actual external-tool comparisons. No single measure answers every research question.

Follow a workflow

Choose a question, then follow the linked example. The connection map shows the inputs, functions and outputs for each route.

Your question Connected workflow
How do scores vary across texts or counting choices? lexdiv_metrics_text_batch() → inspect counts and status → lexdiv_widen() / plot(). Text to report
How do writers, tasks or occasions compare? Tokens + measurement plan → lexdiv_metrics_batch() → planned-observation table → one response per observation. Study tables and models
How frequent, familiar or morphologically varied are the words? Terms + declared reference → word matches and coverage → document summary. Lexical norms, families and affixes
Which words and contexts explain a corpus pattern? Complete annotations → lexdiv_concordance() → positions / lexdiv_collocations(); lexdiv_keyness() → source contexts. Search, keyness
How do I prepare Japanese text? lexdiv_import_annotations() → explicit word selection → diversity or reference profiles. Japanese workflows

Optional reference data

The package code is MIT licensed. Third-party reference data are not bundled. Inspect the terms for the resource you need, then explicitly download it:

lexdiv_resource_info("tubelex")  # source, fixed version, license and size
# After reviewing the linked terms:
lexdiv_download_resources("tubelex", accept_license = TRUE)

The verified cache is reused offline; installation and ordinary calculations do not download data. MorphoLex remains CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, BNC/COCA CC BY-SA 4.0, MorphyNet CC BY-SA 3.0, TUBELEX BSD-3-Clause, and NJ8 has its own permission and attribution terms. Downloading a resource does not change its license.

Cite the version you used 

citation("ldfreq")

Komuro, R. (2026). ldfreq: Reproducible Lexical Diversity and Frequency Profiles (Version 1.0.0) [R package]. Fixed release.

Also cite the selected measurement methods and any reference data you use. See CITATION.cff, license, and release notes.
